Options: Keep Tracksmith if it clears; a screened alternative; the user's own idea
Claude's recommendation: Use Tracksmith for the repo and @tracksmith/* packages now; run trademark, domain and package screening before any public release (the name appears to match an existing running-apparel brand); keep the GitHub repo private until the name is cleared
Needed by: Before the first public release (screening in M0)
Why it matters: Renaming after launch breaks packages, images, domains and user trust

Options: AGPL-3.0 + DCO; GPL-3.0; Apache-2.0; FSL or BSL; CLA
Claude's recommendation: Recommended: AGPL-3.0 with DCO sign-off, one public codebase and an always-free charter. Awaiting user confirmation; the LICENSE file is added once confirmed
Needed by: M0, before the first public release
Why it matters: Public buyers need an OSI licence; AGPL deters closed SaaS forks; DCO keeps contribution friction low

Options: TypeScript end to end; Go + React; JVM; Elixir
Claude's recommendation: TypeScript (Node.js LTS server, React client) in a modular monolith
Why it matters: Client and server share mutation code for optimistic sync; one language keeps many sessions consistent

Options: PostgreSQL only or add MySQL/SQL Server; Postgres full-text or required OpenSearch
Claude's recommendation: PostgreSQL 16+ only (managed variants allowed); Postgres full-text by default with an optional OpenSearch adapter in M2; embedded Postgres for local development
Why it matters: Each extra store multiplies the test matrix and the self-hosting burden

Options: Sync: in-house change log, Zero, ElectricSQL. Authz: OpenFGA co-process, SpiceDB, in-process evaluator
Claude's recommendation: Decide both by M0 spike benchmarks; defaults are the in-house change log and an OpenFGA-style model
Why it matters: They drive perceived speed, offline mode, permission latency and the main security boundary

Options: amd64 only; amd64 + arm64; native Windows server
Claude's recommendation: Linux amd64 and arm64 images; Docker 24+, Podman 4+, Kubernetes 1.28+; tested on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Debian 12, RHEL 9
Why it matters: Defines the install test matrix and the support promise

Options: 1 lane; 3 lanes; 6+ lanes; Workflow fan-out yes or no
Claude's recommendation: 1 lane in M0, 3 lanes from M1; allow Workflow fan-out for well-specified batches
Why it matters: Sets pace and usage cost; more lanes raise merge, CI and review load

Options: Anthropic first; OpenAI-compatible first; no default
Claude's recommendation: Anthropic Claude through the official SDK; claude-opus-5-5 for every feature by default, admin may pick claude-sonnet-5-5 or claude-haiku-5-5 per feature; other adapters and local endpoints supported
Why it matters: Shapes the gateway design, eval suites and the test key needed from M1

Decision: AI on by default once a key is entered
Options: All features on; low-risk features on and agents off; everything off until enabled
Claude's recommendation: Setup asks; preselect summaries, natural language to query, creation help and duplicates; agents and auto-apply stay off; strict mode keeps everything off
Why it matters: Balances usefulness against cost and data-egress surprises

Options: Bundled local model; provider embeddings; both
Claude's recommendation: Bundle a small local embedding model with pgvector; optional provider embeddings through adapters
Why it matters: Duplicates and semantic search must work with no cloud key and in air-gapped installs

Options: Docker Compose + Caddy on a VPS; Helm; single binary; managed PaaS
Claude's recommendation: Compose with PostgreSQL and Caddy (automatic HTTPS) on a VPS by default; Helm values for Kubernetes; no-Docker single binary in M2
Why it matters: Shapes the backend kit, install scripts and the install test matrix

Options: Browser page; CLI; inside the backend setup wizard; all
Claude's recommendation: Static browser page that runs offline (WebCrypto secrets, zips built locally) plus a CLI on the same core; the backend admin area adds origins and rebuilds frontend kits later
Why it matters: Secrets never leave the user's machine; the CLI serves automation and CI

Options: Zip of the static site; single self-contained index.html
Claude's recommendation: Zip by default (cacheable assets, SRI, smaller downloads); single-file index.html as an option for hosts that accept one file
Why it matters: Affects caching, upload effort and integrity checks

Options: Clean URLs with rewrite fallbacks; hash routing
Claude's recommendation: Clean URLs with generated .htaccess, _redirects and nginx fallbacks; the Builder offers hash routing for hosts that cannot rewrite
Why it matters: Wrong choice gives 404s on reload for users of some hosts

Options: Sibling subdomains with SameSite cookies; cross-site OAuth 2.1 PKCE with bearer tokens
Claude's recommendation: Recommend app. and api. subdomains of one site with SameSite cookies; support cross-site with PKCE, short-lived bearer tokens and refresh rotation
Why it matters: Browsers increasingly block third-party cookies; the default must keep logins working

Options: None; opt-in anonymous; opt-out
Claude's recommendation: None by default; opt-in anonymous version and usage ping; zero egress in air-gap mode
Why it matters: Trust with sovereign buyers versus product insight

Options: Always on; toggle in setup; separate download
Claude's recommendation: Separate package, toggle in setup, on by default for imported instances, subject to counsel
Why it matters: Keeps the compatibility layer legally separable while easing migration

Options: Monthly; quarterly; with or without LTS
Claude's recommendation: Minor release every 4 to 6 weeks after 1.0; one LTS per year with 18 months of security fixes; release packages copied to the Drive folder
Why it matters: Sets upgrade burden for self-hosters and backport load for Claude

Options: None; user-run SaaS; partners only
Claude's recommendation: None before 2.0; decide after 1.0 adoption; a SaaS needs SOC 2 and human on-call
Why it matters: A funding option that brings compliance and operations duties Claude cannot carry alone

Options: Donations, support, migrations or hosting; owner-led, company or foundation
Claude's recommendation: Keep every feature free; if revenue is wanted, sell support, migrations and hosting; owner-led with a public charter now, foundation path once several funders exist
Why it matters: Pays for usage, CI and audits without paywalls; avoids the trust damage seen at Plane, Planka and Mattermost

Decision: Counsel review of the clean-room protocol (docs/legal/clean-room.md)
Options: Review by a lawyer the user engages; proceed without review until public release
Claude's recommendation: Proceed with the protocol now; get a one-off review of docs/legal/clean-room.md, ADR-002 and the name screening before the first public release
Why it matters: Compatibility products face copyright, contract and trademark questions; a short review lowers the risk of a forced rewrite
